crime: Every morning her roommate ran laps of the courtyard with her hair tied back in {WITCH_NAME}'s ribbon, borrowed for the purpose. Every evening in their cell, {WITCH_NAME} used her Magic to replay their afternoons around her, with the roommate asleep again on the bunk above.
One lunchtime in the dining hall, the roommate untied the ribbon and handed it back. She had made her own for running.

Years before, {WITCH_NAME}'s older sister had given back everything she had ever borrowed, all in one evening. By morning she was gone. {WITCH_NAME} had known ever since: people give things back before they go.
During the afternoon hours in the cell, she pulled her sleeping roommate headfirst off the upper bunk onto the stone floor.

After the cells were unlocked, the prisoners asked her to replay the cell. She did, and told them it was this afternoon. Around them, she slept on in the lower bunk. Above her, the roommate rolled off in her sleep and lay still exactly where her body was lying now.

Then one prisoner saw the ribbon in the falling girl's hair. It was in {WITCH_NAME}'s own hair now. The prisoners realized they were watching an earlier afternoon, a day when the roommate had fallen and climbed back up into her bunk. This afternoon, only {WITCH_NAME}'s hands had been locked in with her.
fields.epitaph: The ribbon came back to her, and she was the one who left.
fields.epithet: The One Who Hears Goodbye First
execution: In the trial court, the execution stand raises an iron slab with her chained on her back across it. Beside it stands a file of iron girls. One by one they walk past, and each gives something back: an iron keepsake set on her chest, then another, until they lie piled there. The last iron girl lays an iron ribbon on top and walks away. She lies still beneath the pile. No one is left beside the slab.

magic.name: What the Walls Saw
magic.text: She can replay any past moment of the place she's standing in, all around her.
